name: Paneer Butter Masala
subtitle: paneer in a glossy tomato and cashew gravy, sweet with butter and finished with cream

ingredients.note: ripe and red; pale tomatoes give a dull gravy
the body of the sauce, not a garnish
balances the tomato, it should not taste sweet

prepNotes: The gravy is boiled and blended, not fried in the usual bhuna way. That is what keeps it smooth and bright rather than dark.
Soak the cashews properly. Under-soaked nuts leave a grainy sauce that no amount of blending fixes.

steps.text: Simmer the tomato, onion, ginger, garlic, cardamom and soaked cashews with 200ml water for 20 minutes, until everything collapses.
steps.tip: No oil at this stage. It is a stock, not a fry.

steps.text: Cool slightly, blend to a completely smooth puree, then pass it through a sieve. The sieve is what separates this from a home-style curry.
Melt the butter in the pan, add the kashmiri chilli off the heat so it blooms without burning, then pour the puree back in.
steps.tip: Off the heat for the chilli: it scorches in seconds and turns bitter.

steps.text: Simmer 10 minutes until it thickens and the butter shows at the edges. Season with salt and the sugar.
Stir in the paneer and cook 4 minutes, no longer. Add the garam masala, crushed kasuri methi and cream.
steps.tip: Long cooking makes paneer rubbery. It only needs to warm through.

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes off the heat before serving with naan or jeera rice.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. The sauce thickens as it stands, so loosen with a splash of milk or water and reheat gently. Freezing splits the cream.
